memory_lessons.applicability: Use measured tile and CTA configurations as evidence, not as a monotonic scaling rule; hold CTA size fixed when isolating source-tile effects.
memory_lessons.claim: Among the listed valid T1 observations, the compact 128-thread/128-source configuration had the lowest mean time (0.0008998 s). The 256-thread/256-source configuration was slower (0.0009262 s), and the 256-thread/128-source configuration was slower still (0.0011342 s). All passed the 11 correctness cases. These results do not establish how a 128-thread CTA with a 256-source tile will perform.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the proposed 128-thread/256-source configuration with the full correctness suite and official timing metric.

proposal.hypothesis: Keeping a 128-thread CTA, which has the best observed timing among the supplied T1 results, while increasing the compact source tile from 128 to 256 may halve each CTA's tile iterations and barrier pairs. This trades 2 KiB for 4 KiB of shared memory and makes each thread stage two sources per full tile; the official timing must determine whether fewer synchronizations offset those costs.

retained: Use 128 threads per CTA and a 256-entry compact shared-memory source tile, allocating 4096 dynamic shared-memory bytes.
Stage source x, y, z, and mass cooperatively with a thread-strided loop so the 128-thread CTA can load both halves of a full tile.

Keep one target and force accumulator per active thread; synchronize uniformly before reading each tile and before reusing shared memory, bound partial tiles, exclude self-interactions by global index, and write each active output once.
